newsitem.title: CANADA: China gives details of new foreign gold mining law.
newsitem.headline: China gives details of new foreign gold mining law.

text.p: An official with the China Gold Bureau has released details of a new Chinese law governing foreign investment in the country's mining industry.
Yang Dali, chief engineer for the bureau, told a Toronto mining conference on Wednesday that restrictions on foreign involvement in the development of new gold projects will be lessened.
In the past, foreign firms have been limited to working on deposits that were either too difficult for the Chinese to develop themselves or the grade was too poor to make development worthwhile.
These restrictions will be lifted when the new law comes into effect in January, Yang said through a translator.
"Most of the difficulties we perceive in the West are being removed," John Steele, manager for Southeast Asia at Yorkton Securities, said in an interview.
Yang also said a government joint venture with Asia Minerals Corp, a subsidiary of Seattle-based Royal Oak Mines Inc, has received final approval.
"Finally a deal has been signed. This is very profound," said Steele.
He said the deal will encourage the many other companies interested in mining in China.
Yang also suggested China was considering removing a requirement that foreign companies sell their gold to the government for 90 percent of the world price.
While the government accepts gold that is less than pure for that price, "they realize now it's an eyesore in the Western world and they are thinking about changing it," Yang said.
"I think these are the changes we've been waiting for," said Steele.
He said major players such as Toronto-based Barrick Gold Corp should be able to make big gains in China if the changes go through as expected.
"They'll be a major, major player there."
